stimulus_contract.value: v = (r*32 + g) & 0x3FF; four identical 10-bit pixels per 40-bit beat

independent_golden.rule: derived from the frozen contract only (evidence/gen_expected_raw.py); no DUT output, pk_bytes, slot stream or developer intermediate is read
independent_golden.slot_base0_bytes: all zero (legacy base must stay unused)
independent_golden.raw_rule: decompressed bytes == expected_raw.bin byte-for-byte (PRIMARY judged criterion)
independent_golden.frame_bytes_rule: frame_bytes == align_up(stream_len, 4096) and == 4096 (stream_len < 4096; a conformant deflate of 3840 B cannot exceed ~3845 B even with stored blocks)

candidate_bound.note: measured on the frozen r2 TB run; equality is a repeatability/stability check, NOT an independent derivation. Byte equality of the compressed stream is not a valid criterion because a1_deflate_core is a different RFC1950 encoder than CPython zlib.

candidate_bound_prep.note: PREP=1/PRED=1 run of the frozen r2 TB: different transform domain, so only length/adler/header/transport criteria plus raw_crc apply; the compressed length is again candidate-bound.

reference_encoder.why_not_a_criterion: proof from the r1 frozen malformed frame: CPython zlib needs 1391 B, the DUT emitted 3137 B, both with the same Adler-32 0xc49f41ae. The encoder choice (match length/block policy) is an implementation detail; the contract is a legal RFC1950 member that decodes to the exact raw with a correct Adler.

r1_reference_only.note: cross-reference only; never a source of expectation for r2

r3_note: r3 keeps every independent golden value unchanged. The only candidate-bound change is the A1U1 header CRC: r3 starts the per-camera capture identity at 1 (r0d), so frame_id 0->1 and hcrc 5436BF73->A5ECBAD9 (bypass) / 981E85CF->69C48065 (PREP=1/PRED=1). The compressed slot stream itself is unchanged (2470 B / 9909B919).
